cards.back: Many food chains linked together, showing all the feeding links in a habitat.
cards.say: food web. Many food chains linked together, showing all the feeding links in a habitat.

cards.front: Why is a food web better than a food chain?
cards.back: Most animals eat more than one kind of food, and a web shows all of these links.
cards.say: Why is a food web better than a food chain? Most animals eat more than one kind of food, and a web shows all of these links.

cards.back: All the living things of one kind that live in a habitat.
cards.say: population. All the living things of one kind that live in a habitat.

cards.back: All the different populations that live together in a habitat.
cards.say: community. All the different populations that live together in a habitat.

cards.back: A community of living things and the non-living parts of the place where they live.
cards.say: ecosystem. A community of living things and the non-living parts of the place where they live.

cards.back: Depending on each other. Living things in a food web are interdependent.
cards.say: interdependent. Depending on each other. Living things in a food web are interdependent.

cards.front: What may happen if the numbers of a predator drop?
cards.back: Its prey may increase, because fewer are eaten.
cards.say: What may happen if the numbers of a predator drop? Its prey may increase, because fewer are eaten.

cards.front: What may happen to animals if a producer is removed?
cards.back: Animals that eat it have less food, so their numbers may drop, and so do the numbers of the animals that eat them.
cards.say: What may happen to animals if a producer is removed? Animals that eat it have less food, so their numbers may drop, and so do the numbers of the animals that eat them.

cards.back: Catching so many fish that there are not enough left to breed. It can break food webs.
cards.say: overfishing. Catching so many fish that there are not enough left to breed. It can break food webs.

cards.back: Cutting down large areas of forest. It destroys habitats and food sources.
cards.say: deforestation. Cutting down large areas of forest. It destroys habitats and food sources.

cards.front: What happens to animals when their habitat is destroyed?
cards.back: They lose food and shelter, so their numbers drop or they move away.
cards.say: What happens to animals when their habitat is destroyed? They lose food and shelter, so their numbers drop or they move away.

cards.back: A chemical sprayed on crops to kill pests. It can also harm other living things.
cards.say: pesticide. A chemical sprayed on crops to kill pests. It can also harm other living things.

cards.front: How can pesticides harm a food web?
cards.back: They can kill helpful insects, or build up in animals at the top of the food chain.
cards.say: How can pesticides harm a food web? They can kill helpful insects, or build up in animals at the top of the food chain.

cards.back: A living thing brought to a new place where it did not live before. It may harm the animals and plants already there.
cards.say: introduced species. A living thing brought to a new place where it did not live before. It may harm the animals and plants already there.

cards.back: No longer living anywhere on Earth. The dodo is extinct.
cards.say: extinct. No longer living anywhere on Earth. The dodo is extinct.

cards.back: At risk of becoming extinct because there are so few left.
cards.say: endangered. At risk of becoming extinct because there are so few left.

cards.back: Protecting living things and their habitats.
cards.say: conservation. Protecting living things and their habitats.

cards.back: A protected area where wildlife is kept safe.
cards.say: nature reserve. A protected area where wildlife is kept safe.

cards.front: How can people help endangered animals?
cards.back: Protect their habitats, stop hunting, breed them in safe places and set up nature reserves.
cards.say: How can people help endangered animals? Protect their habitats, stop hunting, breed them in safe places and set up nature reserves.

cards.back: The variety of different living things in a place.
cards.say: biodiversity. The variety of different living things in a place.

cards.front: Why is it important to protect rainforests?
cards.back: They are habitats for huge numbers of species and they take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.
cards.say: Why is it important to protect rainforests? They are habitats for huge numbers of species and they take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

cards.front: How does pollution of a river affect the food web?
cards.back: It can kill water plants and animals, so the animals that eat them lose their food.
cards.say: How does pollution of a river affect the food web? It can kill water plants and animals, so the animals that eat them lose their food.

cards.front: What can cause a population to grow?
cards.back: More food, fewer predators, and a safe habitat.
cards.say: What can cause a population to grow? More food, fewer predators, and a safe habitat.

cards.back: Using resources in a way that does not use them up, so they will still be there in future.
cards.say: sustainable. Using resources in a way that does not use them up, so they will still be there in future.
